clue.text: Thackeray's compendium of common cobblers

parts.note: names a collection of sketches by the Victorian novelist Thackeray, with 'cobblers' playing on the old word for a shoemaker, which is also a word for a social climber

explanation.surface: A collection of everyday shoemakers put together by the novelist Thackeray.
explanation.walkthrough: A snob was once a cobbler or shoemaker; Thackeray's book of sketches mocks the other kind, people who look down on those beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray published a satirical series of sketches on social pretension under this title in 1848.

clue.text: Sound your hooter with regret that's a fact!

parts.note: to toot is to sound a car horn

explanation.surface: A driver honks the horn and feels sorry, admitting something is true.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation agreeing that something is undeniably real, as in 'how right you are'.

clue.text: Passed in a timely way, pleased to be reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed anew, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone happy to be reformed after time went by in an orderly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a timely way' extends the definition: time has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has gone by is said to have slipped past or gone.

clue.text: The heavenly hunter on going round Spanish flower

indicators.note: the word on is placed around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; rio is Spanish for river

explanation.surface: A mythical hunter walks around a Spanish bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' reads as a bloom but is a crossword term for a river (it flows).
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation named after the giant huntsman of Greek myth.

clue.text: Advice to the apiarist maintains comforting temperature

explanation.surface: A beekeeper is told how to keep the hive cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the words become an instruction to a beekeeper to hold on to the bees' swarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper is told to retain a cluster of bees; and something that stops heat escaping holds a cosy warmth.

clue.text: See 1
The main source of 24

explanation.surface: Where the sea water comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic name for the sea; 24 down is WATER, and the sea is a great body of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The open sea was called the main in old usage, and the sea is the great reservoir of that liquid.

clue.text: Four-footed folders

parts.note: folders suggests office stationery, but here it means animals that pen flocks into a fold, an enclosure

explanation.walkthrough: A fold is a pen for sheep; these working animals drive the flock into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Farm collies herd sheep into an enclosure called a fold.

clue.text: What's the spinster's game?

parts.note: game hints at a scheme, but the reading is a card game named after an unmarried older woman

explanation.walkthrough: It is a children's card game where the loser is left holding the odd queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional card game whose name is also an old term for an unmarried woman.

clue.text: Tranquilized sitting around 500 in Rome

indicators.note: the word for sitting sits around the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Someone calmed down while sitting about five hundred miles away in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmed with a drug, put under sedation.

clue.text: Short work before a nautical rope become iridescent

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
on a ship, a rope is called a line

explanation.surface: A short piece of work comes before a ship's rope that shimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Opal-like, showing a milky shimmer of changing colours.

clue.text: Concluded, after turning me back, that corrections are made

indicators.note: after turning says the word for concluded follows once the other piece has been turned round
back says the word me is read in the opposite direction, as it is turned

explanation.surface: Someone decides, after turning back, that corrections have been made.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a clause, 'that corrections are made', standing for the past participle: corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: Edited text has had its errors put right.

clue.text: Daybreak characteristic of Nippon

explanation.surface: Dawn, as associated with Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: Nippon is Japan's own name for itself, the land of the dawn, and its flag shows the emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is when the sun comes up; and Japan's emblem and flag show it, the land being so named.

clue.text: Factory equipment found embedded in the garden .

explanation.surface: Machinery turned up buried in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial machinery is called this; and a flower or shrub growing in a bed is one too.

clue.text: … where church officials grows berries

explanation.surface: Continuing the garden: where church officers grow fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on from 12 across; 'church officials' is plural for a singular answer, a looseness of the old clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A presbyterian church office-holder; and a hedgerow tree with black fruit clusters.

clue.text: Money for what one did after the accolade

definitions.text: what one did after the accolade

explanation.surface: Payment for what someone did after being knighted.
explanation.walkthrough: A rose noble was a medieval English gold coin; after the accolade, the tap of a sword in knighting, the new knight stood up a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold coin of Edward IV; and a knight being dubbed got up a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Departed secretly, which could have made Cobden sad

indicators.note: the letters of the words that follow could be made into a new word, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man ran off in secret, which might have upset Cobden.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Cobden was a Victorian free-trade politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away covertly, especially to escape the law.

clue.text: Nautical hazards where the naive seasides may expect to keep money

definitions.text: where the naive seasides may expect to keep money

explanation.surface: Shoals at sea, or where gullible holidaymakers think they can save cash.
explanation.walkthrough: A naive reading takes a seaside's banks to be places for savings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridges of sand under shallow water threaten shipping; and a seaside 'bank' made of sand would be a joke savings house.

clue.text: Paradoxically, he's not the chap to cut out duty

definitions.text: Paradoxically, he's not the chap to cut out duty

parts.words: Paradoxically, he's not the chap to cut out duty
parts.note: the paradox is that excise sounds like cutting out, yet this officer collects the tax rather than removing it

explanation.walkthrough: Excise is a tax on goods; to excise is also to cut out.
explanation.definitionFit: An old customs officer who collected tax on goods such as spirits.

clue.text: A gentle transformation can be graceful

indicators.note: a transformation changes form, so the letters before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gentle change of shape can look lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and refined in appearance or movement.

clue.text: His place of work could be mine

definitions.text: His place of work could be mine

parts.words: His place of work could be mine
parts.note: mine reads as the possessive, but here it is a coal pit

explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks like the pronoun but is a pit where coal is dug.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner works underground in a pit.

clue.text: Cordial drink made neat by the gardener

explanation.surface: A fruit cordial, and something a gardener trims.
explanation.walkthrough: A shrub is also an old drink of fruit juice, sugar and spirit or vinegar.
explanation.definitionFit: An old fruit-and-spirit cordial; and a bush a gardener clips into shape.

clue.text: York o'er topped by this lofty exposed position

indicators.note: the jumbled letters of York o'er sit at the top of trees, and topped signals they are knocked about

explanation.surface: A high windy spot above the city of York.
explanation.walkthrough: Rooks build their nests in a colony high in exposed treetops.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony of rooks' nests in the tops of tall trees, high and windswept.

clue.text: Befuddled, one of the classical nine has retired

indicators.note: has means holds, so the word for retired holds the other piece inside

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night has gone to bed
the nine Muses were the Greek goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: A Muse has withdrawn, feeling confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzled and bewildered, unable to think clearly.

clue.text: Two measures for Dame Terry

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: Two units of measure for a famous actress.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Ellen Terry was a leading Victorian Shakespearean actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name of the actress Dame Ellen Terry.

clue.text: Plenty of space where arms may be stored

explanation.surface: Lots of room, as in an armoury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests weapons, but the second sense is space for your elbows, the joints of your arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom to move; and room for your arm joints to stretch out.

clue.text: Levels the odds

explanation.surface: Making the betting even.
explanation.walkthrough: In betting, evens means odds of one to one.
explanation.definitionFit: Makes flat or equal; and a bookmaker's price where the stake is matched.

clue.text: In law a terribly wet element

indicators.note: in says the letters are inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In legal terms a wet substance is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'laW A TERribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four classical elements, along with earth, air and fire.

clue.text: Friendly question from one with an inferiority complex

definitions.text: question from one with an inferiority complex

explanation.surface: A sociable person and a self-doubter's query.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into three words, the answer is a self-doubting question about one's own capability.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured and agreeable; and an anxious person's query about being capable.

clue.text: Chatters fretfully about rents at variance

indicators.note: at variance means in disagreement, so the letters of the words before are set at odds and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling about rent changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Talks at length idly or grumblingly, as in chatting and griping.

clue.text: Jack gets something to aim at

definitions.note: singular in the clue for a plural answer, a looseness of the old clue

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so tar can stand for jack

explanation.surface: A sailor gets something to shoot at.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and tar are both old words for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects or marks aimed at in shooting.

clue.text: Suffering a bad spell, Dr Yates wandered aimlessly

indicators.note: a bad spell suggests the letters of the doctor's name are badly spelt, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor going through a rough patch roamed without purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Went off course or roamed, losing the way.
